claim: Without an outside signal, asking a model to review and revise its own answer lowers or does not raise accuracy on reasoning tasks (GPT-3.5 CSQA 75.8 to 38.1 at 3 calls; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0). Still holds for the o1 family and DeepSeek-R1 in a blind 'are you sure' pass (Zhang 2025), but Tsui v3 finds the correction blind spot small for reasoning models, so the harm is from unneeded revision.
agent_test: Run S5 revise with and without a code-side trigger at equal tokens on a reasoning set; count right-to-wrong flips.

claim: Apparent gains from self-correction in earlier papers came from oracle labels that decide when to stop; with the oracle GPT-3.5 GSM8K goes 75.9 to 84.3 and GPT-4 HotpotQA 49.0 to 59.0, and the gain vanishes without it.
agent_test: Give the agent the oracle stop signal versus its own stop judgement; measure the gap.

claim: Reflection works when the back-talk comes from outside the model: tests, tools, true error location, a sound verifier (Reflexion ALFWorld 130/134; CRITIC tool vs no tool; Self-Debug up to +12; Stechly sound verifier ~40% vs 16%).
agent_test: Compare revise driven by tool output (test result, count, parse) with revise driven by model critique, same token budget.

claim: Finding the mistake is the bottleneck, not fixing it: given the true error step, backtracking raises accuracy on wrong traces by +18.04 to +43.92 points; a random step gives +5.16 to +21.57; best model finds the first error only 52.87% of the time.
agent_test: Give the agent a located error (from a checker) versus asking it to locate the error; same budget.

claim: Locating errors by plain code (tests, constraint checks) is a better use of calls than model self-critique; self-critique with the same model on graph colouring scored 1 of 100 against a 16% no-critique baseline.
agent_test: Graph colouring or similar with a sound checker; compare critique, checker feedback, and plain resampling.

claim: Plain resampling matches iterative backprompting: on graph colouring, 15 samples at t=1.0 reach about 40%, equal to all four backprompt types; at matched responses, majority vote beat multi-agent debate on GSM8K (88.2 vs 83.0 at 9 responses). Matched-budget code repair against resampling (Olausson 2024) gives modest and uneven gains, 0.97x to 1.05x of baseline in the cells quoted; trained revision with a verifier narrowly beats parallel sampling (Snell 2024).
agent_test: Run best-of-N with a code selector against a revise loop at equal tokens.

claim: Self-reflection can hurt through false positives from self-written tests: Reflexion scored 77.1 vs GPT-4 80.1 on MBPP Python, with a 16.3% false-positive rate versus 1.4% on HumanEval.
agent_test: Count pass-on-fitted-tests that fail held-out checks; require a held-out check before accepting.

claim: Specific, actionable feedback beats generic feedback, which beats none; gains are large on tasks with checkable or stylistic criteria and zero on math where the critic says 'looks good' 94% of the time.
agent_test: Vary feedback specificity from code-generated messages at equal tokens.

claim: Models overturn correct answers when told to self-correct: Llama-3.1-8B lost 20.4 points with 58.8% of correct answers overturned; GPT-3.5 keeps its GSM8K answer only 74.7% of the time.
agent_test: Default to keep the first answer; revise only on a trigger. Measure flip rates.

claim: Fair-prompt, temperature-0 setups show small intrinsic-correction gains, so the sign of the effect depends on prompt wording; the claim 'always harmful' is too strong.
agent_test: Test neutral versus 'find problems' wording of the revise prompt.

claim: Telling a model it was wrong, even without saying why, lifts accuracy on its failed items (GPT-4 0.786 to 0.827 Retry, 0.925 Solution, 0.971 with leaked answer), and more reflection content gives more gain; this requires knowing the first answer failed. In Self-Debug MBPP (GPT-4: 72.8 base, 78.8 with a bare flag, 80.6 with tests) the flag gives most of the gain; Reflexion's own ablations show the written lesson adding 8 points on Rust-50 (0.60 to 0.68, tests-only arm 0.60) and on HotPotQA (100 questions).
agent_test: Compare retry-only with retry plus written lesson, given a code-side failure flag.

claim: Training, not prompting, can create real self-correction (SCoRe MATH second-try delta -11.2 base, +4.4 SCoRe); a cheap prompt-side fix is appending 'Wait' (blind spot cut 89.3%). s1 ablation: after two forced continuations, 'Wait' 53.3 AIME24 vs 'Hmm' 50.0, 'Alternatively' 50.0, none 50.0 (30 questions).
schema_part: none (we do not train); O8 wording
agent_test: Test a neutral 'Wait' continuation marker after a failed check versus no marker.

claim: Experts often see unintended features in their own sketches: in one architect's museum protocol 171 of 606 perceptual actions (28%) were detections of unintended features, and regrouping parts went with them.
agent_test: Log what the output showed beyond the intent; feed it back as an observation. Single case, so low weight.

claim: Attending to parts of an ambiguous drawing roughly doubled interpretations in novices (27.2 vs 44.6 vs 49.6), but groups were self-selected so cause is unclear.
agent_test: Force a re-decomposition of the output into parts before revising; compare with no re-decomposition.

claim: In software design sessions sketches carry the reasoning: over 80% of reasoning activities used sketches, and no sketch was held beyond about 30 seconds; supports an external trace being read back.
agent_test: Keep an external trace of attempts and re-read it at revise time versus summary only.

claim: Reflection-in-action is a descriptive lens, not a tested model: its core studies are single cases with author-coded protocols, and no study tests its predictions with an LLM against human designers.
agent_test: Not testable directly; use the functional pieces above.

claim: Schon's account leans on tacit experience and may narrow the issues considered (Kokotovich 2015, conceptual paper, abstract read); the proposed fix is mapping the problem space before solution work.
agent_test: Add a problem-space map step before revise and test on a task where the first frame is wrong.

claim: When the material is an LLM, back-talk is interpretive and can mislead; designers using ChatGPT reported 'reciprocal reflection-in-action' but 16 of 18 struggled to concretise abstract values.
agent_test: Qualitative only; no agent test beyond noting back-talk must come from code.

claim: Models fail to fix their own errors but fix the same errors when attributed to someone else: 64.5% average blind spot over 14 non-reasoning open models; Claude 3.5 Haiku 52.5%, Claude Sonnet 4 41.4%; reasoning models show a small or negative blind spot (Tsui v3, Aug 2026). 'Wait' brings non-reasoning models near their reasoning siblings (e.g. DeepSeek-V3 0.567 to 0.902 vs R1 0.908).
agent_test: Frame the revise prompt as reviewing a colleague's output versus own output at equal tokens.

claim: In code with unit tests, repair is not clearly better than drawing more samples at the same budget; the clearest wins are the strongest model on the hardest items, and when feedback comes from a stronger model or a human (33.3% vs 52.6% repaired).
agent_test: Same-token comparison on our benchmarks: S5 revise triggered by a code check vs best-of-N plus the same code selector. Open: no frontier-model result.

claim: Revision costs correct answers: a revision-trained model converts about 38% of correct answers to wrong ones without a selector, so the revised and original answers should both stay in the pool.
agent_test: Keep the first answer as a candidate; choose by code check or vote; log how often the revise pass flips a correct answer.

claim: In code, a bare failure flag carries most of the gain from feedback-based retry; the written lesson or explanation adds a few points (Reflexion +8 on two small tests, Self-Debug about +2 over the flag, Renze 0.827 vs 0.876).
agent_test: Three arms at equal calls: retry with flag only, retry with flag plus error text from a program, retry with flag plus a written lesson.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without an outside trigger still lowers accuracy for the o1 family and DeepSeek-R1 in a blind 'are you sure' pass (2025); the evidence for GPT-5-class or Claude thinking models with budgets varied was not found.
agent_test: Run the Huang setup on current frontier models with thinking on and off; report flips of correct answers.

claim: No empirical test of Kokotovich's narrowing claim was found; the nearest measures are looping and over-thinking in refine passes (o1-mini 15.4 'think' steps in failed vs 5.3 in normal cases), which show repetition but not anchoring on a first frame.
agent_test: Measure whether revised answers keep the first answer's frame, with and without a problem-space map step; none is published.

claim: The human back-talk rate (28% of perceptual actions as unexpected discoveries) rests on one architect; Schon's own cases are narrated, not tallied; no multi-designer replication or outcome link was found.
agent_test: Do not use 28% as a target; use only as a descriptive log field.

claim: For open tasks with no checker, no measurement of feedback source was found; the nearest evidence is that a stronger or different critic beats the same model on code, self-preference bias exists in same-model judges, and surveys expect model feedback to work only where checking is easier than making.
agent_test: On an open task, compare self-critique, a different-prompt critic, and a rubric program at equal tokens, judged by blind raters.
